blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The week’s defining development came on Day 29, September 23, when the Senate impeachment court voted 13 to 1 to overturn Presiding Officer Francis Escudero’s original ruling that 16 votes were required to convict Vice President Sara Duterte, deciding instead that the two-thirds constitutional threshold would be computed only from senator-judges legally and factually capable of participating in the trial. With four senators currently excluded, the new denominator of 20 yielded a minimum conviction figure of 14, which Escudero set at that number rather than 13 because 14 exceeds two-thirds while 13 would fall below it.
